clue.text: Duck down

explanation.surface: An order to drop low, or a feather filling.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a sea duck, and its soft breast feathers give the quilt filling called eiderdown, so the bird's name stands for that down.

clue.text: Column leader, for example

parts.note: reads as the person heading a marching column, but is a newspaper piece giving the paper's view

explanation.surface: The officer at the head of a marching file.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's opinion article is called its leader and appears as a column of print.

clue.text: Forceful quality of many CID characters

indicators.note: characters here means letters, which are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Detectives of the Criminal Investigation Department show great drive.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, the plain-clothes detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun this word means an energising force or vigour that drives change.

clue.text: Big guns in some precipitation

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's big guns
taken as written

explanation.surface: Artillery firing during a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: Water falling from clouds as drops is one form of weather moisture.

clue.text: He cheers up dummy

explanation.surface: Someone who lifts spirits, or a silent stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: One who consoles the grieving brings cheer; a baby's dummy pacifier is also called by that name in Britain.

clue.text: An uncomplaining employee who performs the impossible?

definitions.text: An uncomplaining employee who performs the impossible?

parts.words: An uncomplaining employee who performs the impossible?
parts.note: reads as a staff member who never grumbles, but names someone who achieves wonders

explanation.surface: A model member of staff who does what no one else can.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who achieves astonishing results is said to perform wonders beyond nature.

clue.text: None of them believed in getting married or paying debts!

definitions.text: None of them believed in getting married or paying debts!

parts.words: None of them believed in getting married or paying debts!
parts.note: a group who were never wed (O for none, then wed) and who left their bills unpaid

explanation.surface: A band of rebels who rejected marriage and never paid what they owed.
explanation.walkthrough: O (nothing) plus WED describes people not married; the whole word describes money still not paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Money still due to a creditor is outstanding, the state of anyone who refuses to settle bills.

clue.text: Some sort of 29 taking the French for a little run

indicators.note: taking means the first piece gathers up the next one after it

parts.note: 29-across is a ruse, and a trick is one kind of ruse
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A dodge involving the French produces a brief sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: '29' points to the answer of 29-across, DODGE, of which a TRICK is one sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin stream of liquid flows slowly, a small run of water.

clue.text: OK. so you can't be caught out when you're in it

definitions.text: so you can't be caught out when you're in it

explanation.surface: Agreeing, and claiming that the virtuous can't be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'in the right' is to be correct, so nobody can catch you out.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement can be shown with 'correct!'; being in the right means having justice on your side.

clue.text: Taverner's attention drawn by this poor innings (34)

indicators.note: a poor innings is a badly played one, so its letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A publican notices a batsman's feeble score at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: '(34)' is the newspaper's own word count (3,4) misread by the scanner and sitting inside the clue; 'Taverner' is an old word for a tavern keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub hangs a painted board outside to draw customers' eyes, the kind of display a tavern keeper relies on.

clue.text: How Lamb was always tending to be like a ward supervisor

definitions.text: How Lamb was always tending to be

explanation.surface: The essayist's devotion compared to a hospital matron.
explanation.walkthrough: The essayist Charles Lamb spent his life caring for his sister Mary after her breakdown; in Britain the title also names a senior hospital nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb looked after his sibling Mary for decades; the same phrase names a senior nurse in charge of a ward.

clue.text: Winding in a catch that's staggering

explanation.surface: An angler pulling in a fish, and someone tottering about.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler winds line onto the reel to land a fish; a drunk who sways and lurches is said to be doing the same thing.

clue.text: Measures of current resistance to paying postage?

explanation.surface: Electrical units, and a refusal to buy stamps.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is On Her Majesty's Service, printed on British government mail, which travelled without stamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical resistance is measured in units named after Georg Ohm; official government envelopes carried that abbreviation instead of a stamp.

clue.text: Staunch fellow given mortarboard treatment

explanation.surface: A loyal friend, and a graduate's square cap.
explanation.walkthrough: A mortarboard is a builder's board for mortar as well as an academic cap; a builder takes mortar from it to lay each block.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang calls a dependable, generous friend a solid building block; such blocks are the things bedded in mortar.

clue.text: Take off nameless and ugly knits

indicators.note: ugly knits are badly made ones, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without a name: N, the abbreviation for name, is removed from the word knits

explanation.surface: Removing tags from unattractive woollen garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' removes N (name) from KNITS, leaving KITS, which 'ugly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic sketch that mocks someone is a parody, and to parody someone is to send them up.

clue.text: A house conveyor making slow progress

definitions.text: A house conveyor making slow progress

parts.words: A house conveyor making slow progress
parts.note: reads as a removal van stuck in traffic, but means a creature carrying its shell home on its back

explanation.surface: A removal lorry crawling along.
explanation.definitionFit: This garden mollusc carries its shell like a home and is proverbially slow.

clue.text: Medal forged for the wounded in action, perhaps

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military decoration made for soldiers hurt in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier hit in battle may be left crippled, disabled in the legs.

clue.text: Cardinal creation bungled swagger in regardless of feelings

indicators.note: in tells us the swagger word goes inside the jumbled letters
bungled means botched, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: N, north, is one of the four cardinal points of the compass
side is old slang for swagger or putting on airs

explanation.surface: A churchman's project is botched by arrogance, with no thought for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman but is a compass point; 'side' is old slang for putting on airs. The anagram gives INCONRATE before 'in' places the swagger word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thoughtless takes no account of how others feel.

clue.text: Eric's foolishly interrupting poet to give views far above his head

definitions.text: give views far above his head

indicators.note: interrupting means the scrambled letters break into the poet's name

parts.note: Alexander Pope was an English poet

indicators.note: foolishly means the letters behave in a silly way, scrambled

parts.note: the name Eric with its s

explanation.surface: A silly Eric breaks in on a poet to show him a lofty view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eric's' looks like a possessive but its s is fodder; 'foolishly' gives the jumble ERISC, and 'interrupting' places it after the poet's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's sighting tube lets a hidden observer see over obstacles or the surface above.

clue.text: Do a Highland formation dance and make it quick!

explanation.surface: Scottish dancers in step, urged to hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highland fling is a Scottish solo dance; doing it as a group would be dancing the fling in unison.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble something hastily and carelessly is to throw it up in a hurry; dancers performing a fling in unison do the same thing.

clue.text: Only a little backing?

parts.note: backing reads as support, but means placing a bet, here a small one

explanation.surface: Asking whether support offered is only lukewarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wager on a horse is a modest gamble, a little punt.

clue.text: Made some spirited returns to the scene

definitions.text: Made some spirited returns to the scene

parts.words: Made some spirited returns to the scene
parts.note: spirited sounds like lively, but these are ghosts coming back to a place

explanation.surface: Someone going back to a place with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost that keeps revisiting a house troubles it as a spectre.

clue.text: Make a trip to Abraham's hometown

parts.note: taken as written
Ur of the Chaldees is named in Genesis as Abraham's birthplace

explanation.surface: A pilgrim visits the biblical patriarch's birthplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a journey from place to place, and to go on one is to travel.

clue.text: Mechanically wrote on classified material

parts.note: a secret document produced on a keyboard machine, and things sorted into classes

explanation.surface: A clerk producing a secret document on a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing with a keyboard machine produces printed text; things sorted by kind are also categorised this way.

clue.text: Way mother made this pud ding?

definitions.text: Way mother made this pud ding?

parts.words: Way mother made this pud ding?
parts.note: the galaxy name that adds 'Way' to a dairy word, and a pudding mother cooked with plenty of dairy

explanation.surface: A child asking how mum makes her dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pud ding' is 'pudding' split by the scanner; 'Way' completes the galaxy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice pudding made with lots of milk is creamy and white, and the galaxy is named for the same pale look.

clue.text: Taps phone parasites

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Taps phone parasites (4)' gives BUGS twice (taps a phone; parasites), but the answer is printed as DUGS; cannot confirm which is right from crossings.

clue.text: Network used by some ship owners

indicators.note: used by means the letters are being borrowed from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A communications system used by shipping magnates.
explanation.definitionFit: A net is an interlinked web of threads or cords.

clue.text: Dues unsettled? That's not new

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters are moved out of order

explanation.surface: Bills left unpaid are an old story.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have been owned before, so they are not fresh from the shop.

clue.text: And he needs to be, when doc's waiting room

definitions.text: And he needs to be, when doc's waiting room

parts.words: And he needs to be, when doc's waiting room
parts.note: the person sitting in a crowded surgery needs the virtue of waiting calmly, and is named by it

explanation.surface: A person in a busy doctor's waiting room must keep calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under a doctor's care shares a name with the quality of calm waiting they need.

clue.text: A tasty dish to return to behind Sir's back

indicators.note: behind places the to pieces after the turned-round sir
Sir's back means the word sir read backwards

parts.note: the word sir, its 's showing possession

indicators.note: to return means the first word to is turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Going back for more of a delicious meal behind a gentleman's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sir's back' turned gives RIS; 'to return' gives OT; 'behind' places OT and the second 'to' after it, as a dish is said to be served.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock is a savoury, flavourful meal.

clue.text: A nightmare, of course?

parts.note: split nightmare as a 'night mare', a black female horse, found on a racecourse

explanation.surface: Something going badly wrong, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' means on a racecourse, not 'naturally'; a dark horse is an unexpected contender.
explanation.definitionFit: A black racehorse would be a night-coloured mare; the phrase also means a little-known contender who surprises everyone.

clue.text: The ruse of a Venetian magistrate capturing the centre of Padua

indicators.note: capturing means the magistrate holds the next piece inside him

parts.note: the doge was the elected chief magistrate of the Venetian republic

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: A ruler of Venice seizes the heart of a nearby city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the centre of' Padua is D, its middle letter, which 'capturing' puts inside DOGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a crafty trick or scheme for getting out of something.
